quality_guards: Dermatitis risk depends on the substance, concentration, contact duration, wet work, glove choice, skin condition and control performance.
HSE dermatitis guidance is worker-, task-, substance-, exposure-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level health probability.
Lift-truck risk depends on truck type, load, site layout, pedestrian interaction, visibility, maintenance, supervision and operator competence.
HSE lift-truck evidence is vehicle-, site-, operator-, task-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level collision probability.
Ladder risk depends on surface, securing method, work duration, user competence, weather, traffic, public access and ladder condition.
HSE ladder guidance is equipment-, user-, site-, task-, weather-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level fall probability.
Lead risk depends on chemical form, airborne level, ingestion route, task, hygiene, controls, worker factors and exposure duration.
HSE lead evidence is substance-, worker-, task-, exposure-, monitoring-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level toxicity probability.
Compressed-air risk depends on pressure, equipment design, guarding, hose condition, blockage, maintenance, operator behaviour and environment.
HSE compressed-air evidence is system-, equipment-, operator-, maintenance-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level injury probability.
Mpox risk depends on clade, symptoms, contact type, exposure intensity, setting, host vulnerability, controls and timing.
UKHSA mpox evidence is case-, contact-, setting-, clade-, intervention- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level infection probability.
Hepatitis-A risk depends on exposure route, hygiene, food or water contamination, immunity, vaccination, setting and timing.
UKHSA hepatitis-A evidence is person-, contact-, food-, setting-, vaccine-, intervention- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level infection probability.
Food-safety risk depends on product, process, time-temperature control, hygiene, cross-contact, staff practice and consumer susceptibility.
FSA evidence is food-, process-, business-, consumer-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level illness probability.
Medical-device risk depends on device model, software, indication, user, patient, maintenance, environment and incident circumstances.
MHRA reporting evidence is product-, incident-, user-, patient-, investigation- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level harm probability.
Railway risk depends on task, competence, fitness, fatigue, signalling, train and infrastructure condition, protection and operating context.
ORR evidence is worker-, train-, route-, system-, operation-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level rail-incident probability.
Laser-event risk depends on beam power, distance, cockpit exposure, phase of flight, crew composition, visibility and response.
CAA laser evidence is event-, aircraft-, crew-, location-, phase-of-flight- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level aviation probability.
Product risk depends on model, design, manufacture, instructions, use, user group, defect, corrective action and market timing.
OPSS evidence is product-, batch-, user-, market-, enforcement-, corrective-action- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level harm probability.
